The system shall let a dedicated permission grant read-only visibility of the principal records of the other Organizations of the viewer's own Group; records of Organizations outside the Group shall never be visible, and records of another Organization shall never be editable from the viewer's Organization.

The system shall let an OBS node list the people placed in it, each with a standard role and the role played in that node (for example "Engineering lead" in a project team), and shall let an administrator add and remove them.
The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, and Delete on user accounts, including name, email/username, one or more assigned roles, and language preference.
Permission matrix and requirePerm middleware (server/src/rbac.js)

The system shall provide a Permission Matrix screen displaying every permission/capability code against every role, editable by users holding a dedicated permission-management capability, with edits taking effect immediately and platform-wide without a code change.

The system shall enforce every API endpoint, server-side, against the authenticated user's resolved permission set (the union across all assigned roles); a request lacking the required permission shall be rejected with HTTP 403.
The system shall enforce that the Owner and the Evaluator of any two-party verification step are never the same user, both in the UI and at the server.
The system shall provide a minimal user directory (id, name, email) accessible to any authenticated user for assignment purposes, independent of the full user-management permission.

The system shall issue a signed, time-boxed authentication token on successful login, required on every subsequent API call, and shall never expose a stored password hash or credential via any API response.
The system shall expose a single platform-wide justification-required toggle (Section 3.7), defaulting to on, gated by a hierarchy/governance-management capability.

The system shall, when a user opens a screen or deep link that their roles or the Organization's configuration do not allow, show an in-app access notice explaining why and whom to ask, never a blank page or a raw error.

The system shall provide a dedicated permission for viewing the content of individual evaluation or verification verdicts; other users, except the parties to that verification, shall see that an evaluation exists but not its content.

The system shall, at startup, add any permission code introduced by a new release to the catalog together with its default role grants, without overwriting grants an administrator has changed (Section 3.13).

The system shall record, per Organization, exactly one Solution Pack as the single source of truth for that Organization's feature and quota entitlements, defined centrally in one configuration module and consumed by every enforcing route, so entitlements are never duplicated or able to drift between routes.
Entitlements module and configuration screen (server/src/entitlements.js)

The system shall define, for each Solution Pack, at minimum: which modules/features are enabled, the AI tier available (Assistive-only vs. Assistive+Augmented), and numeric ceilings on Projects, OBS nodes, and AI Use Cases.
The system shall record a set of priced Add-Ons, each an independent toggle that grants its associated feature to a Pack that does not already include it standard.
The system shall record a set of priced Compliance & Security Standards modules (at minimum GDPR, ISO/IEC 27001, and SOC 2), each an independent toggle available regardless of Solution Pack.

The system shall, on activating a Compliance & Security Standard, idempotently seed a starting Controls scaffold tagged to that framework, without duplicating it on repeated activation, and shall not delete any Control tagged to a Standard that is later deactivated.

The system shall enforce every Pack-gated feature and every Add-On/Compliance-gated feature server-side via dedicated middleware on the corresponding API route, independently of and in addition to RBAC permission checks; a request for a feature the active configuration does not include shall be rejected with HTTP 403, naming the missing feature.

The system shall expose the Organization's effective configuration and the static Pack/Add-On/Compliance catalog to every authenticated user regardless of role, so client-side navigation can correctly show or hide gated menu items; this read is a UX convenience, not the enforcement boundary.
The system shall expose current usage against every quota dimension, computed live from current data, and shall visually flag a quota that meets or exceeds its allotment.

The system shall never represent, in any UI text, Help content, FAQ answer, or generated document, that activating a Compliance & Security Standard constitutes a certification, an external audit, or a legal attestation of compliance.

The system shall allow an authorized Organization administrator to register, configure, enable, and disable a connection to an external application through the External Integration Registry (Section 3.3), independently of any other registered integration.

The system shall store every external integration's credentials using the same client-side-only or encrypted-server-side pattern already required for the Real LLM Provider Connection (NFR-DA-SEC-07), never in plaintext, and never logged.

The system shall verify an external integration's connection health on demand and shall record the outcome (success, authentication failure, unreachable) with a timestamp, without exposing provider-side error detail that could aid an unrelated attacker.

The system shall allow an authorized administrator to map fields between an external application's records and the platform's own entities, and shall log every inbound or outbound integration transaction (record, timestamp, direction, and result) for audit (Section 4.11).

The system shall accept inbound events from an external application only through the Multi-Channel Communication webhook channel (Section 4.17) or an equivalent authenticated endpoint, never an unauthenticated route, and shall scope every inbound event to the Organization that registered the originating integration.

The system shall support full Create, Read, Update, Delete, and version-revert on an AI Use Case catalog, each entry capturing an id, name, tier (Assistive/Augmented), owning module, trigger, expected output, a human-checkpoint description, and versioned prompt-template content, gated by a dedicated AI-use-case-management capability.
AI Use Case library, activation, overrides and usage log (server/src/services/ai.js)

The system shall seed every Organization with the same library of AI Use Cases on creation, and shall allow an Organization to additionally author custom AI Use Cases up to its active Solution Pack's custom-use-case quota.

The system shall create Version 1 of an AI Use Case automatically on creation, mark it Default/Current, and shall retain the full version history indefinitely; reverting to a historical version shall duplicate its content into a brand-new Current version, never rewrite or delete history.

The system shall allow an Organization Administrator to activate or deactivate any AI Use Case for the whole Organization, and shall allow an authorized Project-level user to set a tri-state (Inherit/On/Off) override per Project; effective activation shall resolve the Project override when set, else the Organization's activation state.

The system shall block, server-side, any new AI suggestion from a deactivated AI Use Case (by its effective state) immediately on deactivation, while never retroactively hiding or removing content a human already reviewed and approved before deactivation.

The system shall visually label every AI-generated output, wherever shown, as AI-generated and requiring human review, alongside its tier and its generation source (deterministic built-in engine or a configured live model).

The system shall write an append-only AI Usage Log entry for every AI suggestion's outcome (Accepted, Edited, or Rejected), capturing the use case, Organization, Project, the record it applied to, the acting user, and a timestamp; the log shall expose no edit or delete route.

The system shall allow a user to configure a Real LLM Provider Connection (provider, model, endpoint, API key) that is persisted client-side only, is forwarded once per generation request, is never returned in any API response, never written to any log, never cached or persisted server-side beyond that single request, and is never included in any data export.

The system shall, on any failure of a live LLM call, fall back automatically to the AI Use Case's deterministic built-in generator, so a misconfigured or unreachable connection never blocks a suggestion from being produced.
The system shall ensure an AI Use Case's activation, tier, or generation never grants a user visibility into data beyond what their RBAC role and permissions already allow.

The system shall, before generating any suggestion, ground it in retrieved reference content (Section 4.5), instruct the underlying model to stay within the application's own vocabulary, and state no number, score, or name not present in the retrieved references or the record's own data; the retrieved references shall be disclosed to the user alongside the output.
